meta.title: Izanagi AI — The runtime that orchestrates engineering agents
meta.description: Agent and skill framework for autonomous software engineering: 21 specialized agents, adaptive routing, evaluation, self-healing and persistent memory.

hero.eyebrow: INTENT · CONTEXT · SKILLS · AGENTS · EXECUTION · VALIDATION · MEMORY · EVOLUTION
hero.subtitle: One line of intent becomes context, skills and agents in motion — validated, remembered, folded back into the system that built it.

problem.body: A prompt is not a plan. Without structure, without evaluation and without memory between runs, every task starts from a blank page — and repeats the same mistakes.

intent.body: You say what you want, once, in plain language. Izanagi reads the request against your codebase, your conventions and your history — because intent without context is just a guess dressed up as a plan.

whatIsIt.body: Five layers stand between what you asked for and what ships — each one a gate the work has to earn its way through.

routing.title: Context & Routing
routing.desc: Reads the task against your repo and picks the exact agent and skills it calls for — no manual wiring.

orchestration.title: Agents in Motion
orchestration.desc: Composes the chosen skills and agents into a live execution graph and runs it end to end.

evaluation.title: Validation
evaluation.desc: Nothing ships unchecked — every delivery is scored against weighted metrics and an objective verdict.

healing.title: Self-Healing
healing.desc: Failures surface at runtime and get corrected in the same run, not in a follow-up ticket.

memory.title: Memory
memory.desc: What failed, and why, is kept — so the next run starts smarter, not from zero.

evolution.body: Nothing that happens in one run is wasted. It feeds back into the next — routing gets sharper, skills get curated, the whole structure reorganizes around what actually works.

evolutionTimeline.title: The framework's own version history.
evolutionTimeline.body: Every release below is real — pulled straight from the izanagi-ai package's GitHub releases. Major jumps mark actual architectural shifts, not marketing milestones.

architectureExplorer.title: Five layers. One closed execution loop.
architectureExplorer.body: izanagi-ai ships as a real layered runtime, not a stack of prompt templates: every task is classified and routed, planned into an executable graph, evaluated against weighted metrics, healed on failure, and remembered across sessions. Select a layer to see the actual engine files, agents and CLI commands behind it.

sectionLabels.empty: Select a layer above to inspect its engines, agents and CLI surface.

routing.name: Routing
routing.tagline: Classify the task, pick the model, select the chain.
routing.body: Every interaction enters through the Decision Engine, which classifies input into one of 15 task categories — new_project, bug, refactor, security_audit, review, optimize, teach and more — with a 90% confidence target before anything executes. Below 70% confidence, the engine flags the input as uncertain and asks for clarification instead of guessing. Once classified, the task is matched to a skill chain in the Skill Chain Matrix and handed to the Skill Composer, which resolves the matching domain composition from core/skill-resolver.json rather than activating skills in isolation. In parallel, the Model Router scores candidate models on relevance (weight 0.40), historical success (0.20), compatibility, risk, cost and latency, then assigns a tier — fast, balanced or premium — so a simple question never burns a premium model unnecessarily.

decisionEngine.name: Decision Engine
decisionEngine.description: Entry point of every interaction. Classifies input into a task category, validates skill-chain dependencies before execution, and enforces the token budget at routing time.

modelRouter.name: Model Router & Adaptive Routing
modelRouter.description: Selects the model per task by complexity, reasoning requirement, risk, cost, latency and context window across three tiers: fast, balanced, premium.

orchestration.name: Orchestration
orchestration.tagline: Turn the chosen chain into an executable graph.
orchestration.body: The Planning Engine breaks the task into atomic steps — never more than one file or 50 lines each — estimates effort per step, and orders them with a topological sort so dependencies are respected before any code is written. The Execution Graph then turns that plan into an explicit DAG built dynamically for the task (never a giant static workflow), using node kinds like agent, skill, tool, validator, evaluator, aggregator, parallel and gate. Templates already exist for common shapes — fullstack (discovery → architect → security ∥ database ∥ product → senior-engineer → qa-gate ∥ critic → evaluation), debugging, security_audit, frontend and more — and the planner computes parallel batches wherever nodes have no mutual dependency. Underneath it all, the Skill Composer enforces output→input chaining across 12+ domain compositions (web_cinematic, webgl_experience, api_backend, fullstack_crud, debug_session, refactor_safe...): a skill loaded outside its domain chain is a banned anti-pattern.

planningEngine.name: Planning Engine
planningEngine.description: Decomposes any task into atomic, dependency-ordered steps with effort estimates before a single line of code is written.

executionGraph.name: Execution Graph & Orchestration
executionGraph.description: Builds a dynamic DAG per task with typed nodes, retry policies, timeouts and per-node token budgets; computes parallel execution batches.

skillComposer.name: Skill Composer
skillComposer.description: Resolves domain compositions from core/skill-resolver.json and chains skills so each artifact feeds the next — isolated 'decorative' skills are forbidden.

evaluation.name: Evaluation
evaluation.tagline: Score the result, don't just trust it.
evaluation.body: The Evaluation Engine scores every artifact against eight weighted metrics — correctness (0.30), test results (0.20), requirement coverage (0.15), architecture, security, performance, maintainability and artifact validity — and derives one of five verdicts: PASS (score ≥ 0.85, zero failing tests), PASS_WITH_WARNINGS, FAIL, BLOCKED or UNKNOWN. Before that score is even reached, every output already passed through six Quality Gates: Security (fatal — blocks output outright), Style, Clarity, Conciseness, Completeness, and a sixth Masterpiece & High-Craft gate that is fatal for visual and architecture work — rejecting generic AI-slop, broken reference fidelity, or any stub/placeholder code. After delivery, the Reflection Engine runs a structured self-review over a rolling window of the last 50 tasks, scoring quality, process, security and teaching, and forwards any detected pattern to the Evolution Engine.

evaluationEngine.name: Evaluation Engine
evaluationEngine.description: Weighted-metric scoring engine that derives a PASS / PASS_WITH_WARNINGS / FAIL / BLOCKED / UNKNOWN verdict for every agent or workflow output.

qualityGates.name: Quality Gates
qualityGates.description: Six sequential gates — Security, Style, Clarity, Conciseness, Completeness, Masterpiece & High-Craft — with Security and Masterpiece both fatal on failure.

reflectionEngine.name: Reflection Engine
reflectionEngine.description: Post-task self-review over a rolling 50-task window; detects recurring mistakes and token-waste patterns and feeds them to the Evolution Engine.

healing.name: Healing
healing.tagline: Classify the failure, recover, never loop forever.
healing.body: When a Quality Gate or a verification command fails, Self-Healing & Failure Memory classifies the failure into one of seven types — recoverable (timeout, 429, 5xx), validation, planning, tool, agent, dependency or non-recoverable — and applies the matching strategy: exponential-backoff retry, corrective skill replacement, a full replan, or a handoff to the responsible agent (devops, techlead, bug-hunter). Hard limits on attempts, tokens and total time guarantee the loop always terminates, aborting with a report rather than spinning forever. The Checkpoint & Self-Healing Swarm Engine extends this with persistent state checkpoints for time-travel debugging and a test-fix loop: it captures the exact stack trace, injects it directly into the responsible specialist's context, generates the corrective patch, and re-runs verification autonomously until the build is green — no human in the loop for routine failures.

selfHealing.name: Self-Healing & Failure Memory
selfHealing.description: Classifies failures into 7 types and applies the matching recovery strategy; consults known failure patterns via findRelevantFailures() before every execution.

checkpointSwarm.name: Checkpoint & Self-Healing Swarm Engine
checkpointSwarm.description: Persists intermediate state for time-travel resume, and runs autonomous capture → inject → patch → revalidate loops until tests pass.

memory.name: Memory
memory.tagline: Never solve the same problem twice.
memory.body: The Context Engine builds a minimal, high-signal context window per task — system, project, memory and task sections, each with its own token ceiling — scoring every candidate memory item for relevance before deciding whether to load it in full, as a compressed summary, or not at all. When usage crosses 70% of budget, the Compression Engine and Token Manager take over: four escalating levels (lossless, light, aggressive, emergency) shrink token count while a hard rule preserves security decisions and action items in full, no matter how aggressive the compression. The Evolution Engine watches the Reflection Engine's output for recurring patterns and — once a mistake repeats 3+ times — proposes a concrete skill or chain update, auto-applying patches but requiring explicit approval for anything structural. Every run is traced end-to-end into .izanagi/state/traces, and durable lessons persist as append-only entries in .agents/memoria/ (contexto.md, decisoes.md, erros-corrigidos.md, learnings.md) — the exact anti-repetition memory the Skill Composer's Study-First phase reads before any new task starts.

contextEngine.name: Context Engine
contextEngine.description: Builds the minimal high-signal context window per task and compresses it under a strict token budget before delivering it to the executor.

compressionEngine.name: Compression Engine
compressionEngine.description: Four escalating compression levels (lossless → emergency) that cut token count while guaranteeing zero loss of security items and action items.

tokenManager.name: Token Manager
tokenManager.description: Tracks and budgets every token across soft (2048), hard (4096), context (8192) and emergency (512) tiers, triggering compression at 70% usage.

evolutionEngine.name: Evolution Engine
evolutionEngine.description: Turns reflection patterns into skill/chain updates once a mistake recurs 3+ times; auto-applies patches, requires approval for structural changes.

tracing.name: Tracing & Observability
tracing.description: Records every execution — tokens, retries, failures, spans, evaluation verdict — to .izanagi/state/traces/<run-id>.json for full replay.
